ai.title: Fix chat resume ranking and add network retry for agent validation
ai.summary: The `--continue` flag now resumes the correct chat session by ranking saved chat files rather than directory modification times, preventing the empty log directory created at launch from being selected. In the SDK, remote agent validation now retries the HTTP POST once when Bun reuses a closed socket after idle, using `isTransientNetworkError` to detect transient failures. These two fixes address a bug where the newest directory was always the current launch's log folder, and a flaky network issue that blocked CLI sends after idle periods.
ai.evidence: In `cli/src/project-files.ts`, `getMostRecentChatDir` now ranks chat directories by the `mtimeMs` of `run-state.json` or `chat-messages.json` instead of the directory mtime. In `sdk/src/validate-agents.ts`, the remote fetch is wrapped in a `post` helper that retries once via `isTransientNetworkError`.

changes.what: Updated `getMostRecentChatDir` to rank chats by saved file mtime instead of directory mtime so `--continue` skips the empty launch log directory.
Added single-attempt retry for transient network errors in `validateAgents` remote validation to handle socket reuse after idle.

eli5.text: Choosing to continue a previous conversation now looks at the last time chat files were actually saved, instead of the date the folder was last opened, so the empty folder created by the current launch no longer tricks the system into skipping your real work. The developer toolkit also tries one extra time if a network connection drops while checking agent settings, preventing a temporary blip from blocking your next message. These fixes affect developers using the command-line assistant, improving the accuracy of session resumption and the reliability of background checks after periods of inactivity.

entries.title: SDK update: run-terminal-command

ai.title: SDK terminal command disables detached spawn on Windows
ai.summary: The `spawnDirectTerminalCommand` function in the SDK now sets the detached option to true only on POSIX systems, explicitly excluding Windows. On Windows, the process is no longer detached because the `DETACHED_PROCESS` flag would cause child console programs to spawn visible windows; instead, the host relies on `windowsHide` and taskkill for process tree management. This change prevents the creation of new visible console windows when running terminal commands on Windows.
ai.evidence: In `sdk/src/tools/run-terminal-command.ts`, the `spawnDirectTerminalCommand` function changes the detached spawn option from a hardcoded boolean to a platform check `os.platform() !== 'win32'`.

eli5.text: The assistant no longer runs background tasks in a separate, hidden window on computers using Windows operating systems. This fix is for users running the free coding tool on Windows, stopping blank program windows from flashing onto their screen while the assistant works. Your daily use is unaffected, except that you will no longer see these unexpected pop-ups.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: log-ingest

ai.title: Cap client log timestamp skew in Axiom ingest
ai.summary: Client log timestamps that deviate from the server's receive time by more than one hour are now overwritten with the server time in the `common` package. The mechanism relies on a new `MAX_CLIENT_CLOCK_SKEW_MS` constant used in the `buildLogRows` function to compare the client's timestamp against the current time. This change addresses an Axiom support issue where client clocks set to 1976 or 2097 widened block time ranges, causing every query to read those blocks.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/util/log-ingest.ts`, `buildLogRows` now computes `clientTs` and replaces it with `now` if `Math.abs(clientTs.getTime() - now.getTime()) > MAX_CLIENT_CLOCK_SKEW_MS`. This is backed by a new constant `MAX_CLIENT_CLOCK_SKEW_MS` set to one hour, and a new test in `common/src/util/__tests__/log-ingest.test.ts` that asserts timestamps from 1976 and 2118 are replaced with the server's `now`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not specify which client environments were most prone to the 1976 or 2097 clock skew.

eli5.text: The service now replaces any client log time that is more than an hour off from the server's current time with the server's time. This prevents wrong or stuck clocks from stretching the time range that internal queries must scan, which was slowing down log searches. No changes are needed, and this has no visible effect on how the tool works for you.
